item.title: Cost of Living in Truganina Melbourne

Is Truganina Expensive?

Truganina sits somewhere in the middle of Melbourne’s cost spectrum. It’s not cheap, but it’s not going to break the bank either — assuming you’re realistic about expectations.

The cost of living here reflects what the suburb offers. Location, community, access to amenities — you get what you pay for, and in Truganina, you’re generally getting good value for the price point.

Getting Around Truganina — The Quick Version

Public transport in Truganina is decent. You can get to the city in roughly 30 to 50 minutes during peak hours. Having a car helps, especially for weekend errands and trips outside the PT network.

Train Access

Truganina is served by train, though you may need to get to the nearest station which can be a short walk or bus ride away.

item.title: Truganina — History and How It's Changed
item.description:
If walls could talk in Truganina, they would tell stories spanning over a century of Melbourne evolution.

See our full Truganina suburb guide for the current picture.

What Truganina Was Originally

Before it was what you see today, Truganina was agricultural land and market gardens. The original residents built the suburb’s foundation — the street grid, the housing stock, the community institutions that still exist in some form.

Like most of Melbourne, Truganina’s history is inseparable from the broader story of a city that grew outward from the Yarra in waves. This suburb was settled when Melbourne needed it — whether for housing workers, accommodating families, or providing a retreat from the city centre.

item.title: Truganina Neighbourhood Guide — Streets and Pockets
